Job Description
Analysts and Reporters develop targets and plans in support of Operations in the Information Environment (OIE); collect, analyze, and fuse target
communications and multiple source information to identify Essential Elements of Information (EEI) in order to map and develop target networks, and
conduct geospatial analysis; access and manipulate databases; perform mission planning and fusion analysis; provide Signals Intelligence (SIGINT)
trend analysis; and draft, disseminate, and sanitize SIGINT reports, cryptologic mission reports, and cryptologic and multiple source assessments to
meet Fleet, Joint, and National requirements.

common_text: Cryptologic Technicians (Collection) (CTR) operate advanced computer systems to conduct Operations in the Information Environment (OIE) and support Cyberspace Operations; and collect, analyze, and exploit Signals of Interest (SOI) throughout the Radio Frequency (RF) spectrum to identify, locate, and report worldwide threats to provide Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Counter Command, Control, Communications, Computer, and Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance, and Targeting (C-C5ISRT), Indications and Warning (I&W), Counter Unmanned Systems (C-UxS), targeting, tactical, and digital network support to Warfare Commanders and National consumers supporting surface, subsurface, air, space, and special operations forces to maintain information superiority. . __________________________________________

Cryptologic Technicians (Collection) (CTR) operate advanced computer systems to conduct Operations in the Information Environment (OIE) and support Cyberspace Operations; and collect, analyze, and exploit Signals of Interest (SOI) throughout the Radio Frequency (RF) spectrum to identify, locate, and report worldwide threats to provide Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Counter Command, Control, Communications, Computer, and Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance, and Targeting (C-C5ISRT), Indications and Warning (I&W), Counter Unmanned Systems (C-UxS), targeting, tactical, and digital network support to Warfare Commanders and National consumers supporting surface, subsurface, air, space, and special operations forces to maintain information superiority. . __________________________________________

Analysts and Reporters develop targets and plans in support of Operations in the Information Environment (OIE); collect, analyze, and fuse target communications and multiple source information to identify Essential Elements of Information (EEI) in order to map and develop target networks, and conduct geospatial analysis; access and manipulate databases; perform mission planning and fusion analysis; provide Signals Intelligence (SIGINT) trend analysis; and draft, disseminate, and sanitize SIGINT reports, cryptologic mission reports, and cryptologic and multiple source assessments to meet Fleet, Joint, and National requirements.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
